title: Platform Engineering: Kernel eBPF Telemetry & Workload Identity Federation
summary: Covers kernel-level network tracing with <1% overhead, OpenTelemetry W3C trace context, and MAS TRM Section 9 credential removal.

ai.title: Teacher-Student Knowledge Distillation for Edge SLM Inference
bullets: Compact Model Specialization: Distills reasoning capabilities from 70B teacher models into 3B small language models (SLMs) for on-device deployment.
Logit & Feature Alignment: Optimizes student models using Kullback-Leibler divergence loss on intermediate transformer attention layers.
Sub-50ms Edge Execution: Runs quantized 4-bit models locally on edge devices with under 2GB RAM footprint.
ai.interview_framing: Discuss how distilling frontier models into task-specific SLMs reduces cloud inference API costs by 90% while providing offline capabilities.

cloud.title: Sidecarless Ambient Service Mesh vs Traditional Envoy Injection
bullets: Layer 4 ztunnel Proxying: Node-level zero-trust tunnel proxies handle mTLS encryption and identity attestation with near-zero latency overhead.
Layer 7 Waypoint Proxies: Dynamically provisions standalone Envoy proxies only for namespaces requiring advanced HTTP routing or authorization policies.
Simplified Upgrade Lifecycle: Eliminates pod restarts during service mesh version upgrades.
cloud.interview_framing: Contrast Istio Ambient mesh with traditional sidecar proxies, emphasizing how separating Layer 4 transport from Layer 7 policy simplifies day-2 operations.

data.title: Apache Flink Statefun & Exactly-Once Stateful Stream Processing
bullets: Chandy-Lamport Checkpointing: Periodically snapshots distributed streaming state to object storage with sub-second alignment barriers.
RocksDB State Backend: Manages terabyte-scale streaming state out of RAM to prevent JVM garbage collection pauses.
Exactly-Once Two-Phase Sinks: Coordinates with transactional Kafka sinks to guarantee no duplicate processing during worker recovery.
data.interview_framing: Explain the mechanics of Flink distributed checkpointing and how it guarantees exactly-once processing semantics for financial fraud detection pipelines.

sec.title: Zero-Trust SPIFFE/SPIRE Attestation & MAS TRM Section 9 Compliance
bullets: Cryptographic cgroup Attestation: Validates container process binary paths, namespaces, and Kubernetes tokens directly inside the Linux kernel.
Ephemeral SVID Credential Injection: Delivers X.509 certificates to workloads via UNIX domain sockets, removing database passwords from environment variables.
MAS TRM Section 9.2 Compliance: Meets strict regulatory mandates for end-to-end mTLS encryption and automated 60-minute secret rotation.
sec.interview_framing: Explain how SPIFFE eliminates shared static passwords in financial institutions, drastically reducing the blast radius of container compromises.

devops.title: Kernel eBPF Socket Tracing & OpenTelemetry W3C Distributed Context
bullets: Low-Overhead Packet Inspection: eBPF programs hook directly into kernel network tracepoints with <1% CPU overhead.
Automatic Distributed Tracing: Inspects and propagates W3C trace-context headers across HTTP and gRPC calls without manual code instrumentation.
Continuous Profiling: Captures on-CPU and off-CPU flame graphs across all running containers to pinpoint production bottlenecks.
devops.interview_framing: Articulate how eBPF observability provides complete system visibility with negligible overhead, reducing Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) during outages.

arch.title: Distributed Multi-Master Database Replication & CRDT Conflict Resolution
bullets: Conflict-Free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs): Automatically resolves concurrent write conflicts across multi-region databases without distributed locks.
State-Based vs Operation-Based CRDTs: Compares network bandwidth trade-offs between full state replication and delta mutation streams.
High Availability Under Partitions: Guarantees AP (Availability + Partition Tolerance) properties under CAP theorem constraints.
arch.interview_framing: Discuss when to choose CRDTs over consensus protocols, citing real-world examples like collaborative documents and shopping cart counters.

finops.title: Cross-AZ Data Transfer Optimization & PrivateLink Architecture
bullets: Availability Zone Colocation: Schedules chatty microservices within the same Availability Zone using Kubernetes pod affinity to eliminate cross-AZ transfer fees.
AWS VPC Endpoints & PrivateLink: Routes traffic to S3 and DynamoDB over internal AWS networks, avoiding internet NAT gateway data processing costs.
Egress Cost Monitoring: Tracks network egress volume per Kubernetes namespace using Prometheus and OpenCost.
finops.interview_framing: Show how optimizing network topology and replacing NAT gateways with VPC endpoints cuts cloud networking bills by up to 50%.

sources.title: AWS Best Practices for Data Transfer Costs

gov.title: Automated EPSS Vulnerability Prioritization & VEX Attestations
bullets: Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS): Focuses remediation efforts on CVEs with high probability of real-world exploitation rather than raw CVSS scores.
Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange (VEX): Generates machine-readable attestations confirming whether a vulnerable library is reachable in runtime execution.
Automated CI/CD Gate Enforcement: Blocks production deployments only when exploitable vulnerabilities are actively detected.
gov.interview_framing: Explain how combining EPSS scores with VEX runtime reachability reduces vulnerability triage noise by 80% while strengthening security posture.

flashcards.question: How does eBPF-based observability differ from traditional sidecar proxy telemetry (e.g., Envoy)?
flashcards.answer: eBPF runs bytecode directly inside the Linux kernel, capturing socket and network metrics across all pods on a node with <1% CPU overhead, eliminating sidecar memory bloat and context-switch latency.

full_articles.devops:
Title: Kernel-Level Observability with eBPF and OpenTelemetry
Source: eBPF Foundation & CNCF (2026)

Section 1: The Overhead of Sidecar Proxies.
Injecting Envoy sidecars into thousands of microservice pods consumes gigabytes of memory and adds 2-5ms hop latency. eBPF hooks into kernel socket buffers directly, observing all TCP handshakes with near-zero overhead.
